etymologies.etymologyHTML: blues (countable and uncountable, plural blues)

definitions.definition: (informal, in the singular or in the plural) One's particular life experience, particularly including the hardships one has faced.
(informal, in the singular or in the plural) The negative emotional state produced by a particular action, occupation, experience, or idea.
(usually in the plural, informal) A feeling of sadness or depression.

quote.citation: 1881–1882, Robert Louis Stevenson, Treasure Island, London; Paris: Cassell & Company, published 14 November 1883, →OCLC:
quote.text: If we had been allowed to sit idle we should all have fallen in the blues  […]

definitions.definition: (music, in the singular) A musical composition following blues forms.
(music) A musical form, African-American in origin, generally featuring an eight-bar or twelve-bar blues structure and using the blues scale.
A uniform made principally of a blue fabric, and especially a full dress uniform thus colored.

quote.text: You never planned on the bombs in the sandOr sleeping in your dress blues.

definitions.definition: (drug slang) Any of various blue pills sold on the street, mimicking the appearance of prescription pain killer tablets.
third-person singular simple present indicative of blue
